criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission concept addresses a relevant Australian problem (GBR coral bleaching) with defined users. However, it lacks quantitative system requirements, detailed instrument specs, and payload trade-offs.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The Gantt chart and task list logically map project milestones across relevant orbital design topics, but omit contingencies, buffers, and schedule risk mitigation.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is limited to completing basic software tutorials and literature review; no actual preliminary technical calculations, orbital parameters, or mission-specific simulation results are presented.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report is clearly written and logically ordered, but all references are presented as unformatted bare URLs, and the Gantt chart lacks formal captioning and numbering.

technical_issues.issue: No quantitative technical requirements (e.g., spatial resolution target, spectral bands, revisit frequency) are specified.
Lacks preliminary engineering calculations, orbital parameters (altitude, inclination, COEs), or STK simulation outputs.
Citations and source references are provided as bare URLs without formal bibliographic formatting.

overall: A well-motivated concept addressing Great Barrier Reef monitoring with a clear plan and software selection. To improve, include quantitative mission requirements, preliminary orbital calculations or simulation outputs, contingency planning, and standard bibliographic references.

feedback.summary: You have established a well-motivated space mission concept targeting Great Barrier Reef monitoring, supported by a structured project plan and clear software selection. Your rationale clearly identifies target users. To reach higher rubric levels in the final report, define quantitative engineering requirements, provide preliminary orbital calculations or simulation outputs, build contingency buffers into your schedule, and adopt standard academic citation practices.
next_steps: Define quantitative mission and payload requirements in your concept section, such as target spatial resolution, spectral bands, and revisit frequency for reef monitoring.
Conduct and document preliminary technical calculations or STK simulation outputs, specifying orbital parameters (altitude, inclination, and classical orbital elements).
Update your Gantt chart with schedule contingency buffers, number and caption all figures, and convert the bare URLs into formal bibliographic citations.

criteria.C1: In "Mission Concept & Rationale", you established a compelling Australian mission context for coral bleaching and identified key user groups. To achieve "Accomplished", provide complete, quantitative mission requirements—such as target revisit rates, spatial resolution, and spectral bands—and justify your payload selections with references to literature.
criteria.C2: In "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress", your Gantt chart and task descriptions logically map out key orbital design milestones. To advance to "Accomplished", make your plan robust by incorporating explicit contingency buffers, identifying potential project risks, and explaining how your workflow accommodates schedule variations.
criteria.C3: Completing initial STK tutorials (1–4) and literature review shows a good start in "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress". To reach "Accomplished", provide preliminary mission-specific engineering results, such as baseline orbital parameters (altitude, inclination, COEs), initial coverage analysis, or early simulation plots with brief interpretations.
criteria.C4: Your report is clearly written with a logical document structure. To reach "Accomplished", ensure all graphical elements—such as your Gantt chart—have formal figure numbers and captions, and replace the bare URLs in "Useful Links" with complete, properly formatted bibliographic references cited in-text.
